🚔📊 Israel’s Top Party for Personal Security

A recent HaMadad survey, analyzed by Shmuel Rosner, placed Otzma Yehudit first among parties Israelis associate with fighting crime and improving personal security. The underlying crosstabs, sample details, field dates, and margin of error were not available in the material reviewed, so the finding should be treated as a reported poll result rather than a complete measurement of public opinion.

The party’s leader is National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, who has held the portfolio since December 2022.

Crime and violence remain a central problem, especially in Arab communities. The Abraham Initiatives has recorded 151 Arab citizens killed in crime- and violence-related incidents in Israel so far in 2026, according to figures cited in recent coverage. 

Ben-Gvir can point to policies that are highly visible to his voters: looser gun-licensing rules, tougher prison conditions for Palestinian security detainees, and a campaign against unlicensed construction. His political advantage is the ability to sell public anxiety back to the people who feel it.

A separate and stronger claim is the demolition count.

Ben-Gvir announced this week that authorities had demolished their 10,000th “illegal structure” during his enforcement drive. The milestone was marked in Juarish, a neighborhood in Ramla. The ministry’s wording referred to structures across the country, a category that can include permanent buildings, shacks, caravans, tents, and agricultural enclosures. 

In a response to criticism, Ben-Gvir said he had demolished 10,000 “houses” in the Negev in the past year and a half. The claim is broader than his ministry’s own announcement in two ways: it turns nationwide structures into homes, and relocates the entire count to the Negev.

Those are not interchangeable figures. The improvement in enforcement may be real. The political number is doing more work than the underlying category can support.

Ben-Gvir has also made political symbolism central to his public appeal: his past portrait of Baruch Goldstein, the noose imagery used by his circle, and his promotion of capital punishment for people convicted of terrorism. A death-penalty bill does not itself specify hanging, and the proposed execution facility is a separate policy initiative. 

The poll returns us to the same question. Israelis may rank Otzma Yehudit highest on personal security not because crime has fallen under Ben-Gvir, but because he has made fear, punishment, and visible force the clearest product on offer.

📣 EU to revise MiCA rules in 2027 amid US stablecoin push 

⚠️ European Union officials are preparing to revise the bloc’s MiCA crypto framework in 2027 as foreign stablecoin restrictions and faster U.S. rulemaking expose gaps in the existing regime. The planned revision would examine how MiCA treats stablecoins issued outside the European Union. Current requirements have prevented several foreign issuers from receiving authorization, limiting their access to regulated exchanges across the bloc.

💬 “Reopening the file seems unavoidable at this stage,” an unidentified European diplomat told Euronews.

🔗 The diplomat cited positions taken by European institutions, including the European Central Bank, along with changes in global regulation and digital-asset technology. No final proposal has been published. Any amendment would need to pass through the EU’s legislative process before taking effect. The consultation covers developments that have occurred since MiCA entered into application. Its deadline has been extended to Sept. 30, with crypto issuers, service providers, regulators, central banks and finance ministries invited to respond.

🌍 Pezeshkian administration backed Armed Forces during 12-day and 40-day wars

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The administration of President Masoud Pezeshkian has sought to place the country’s executive capacities at the service of national defense during the 12-day and 40-day wars, emphasizing support for the Armed Forces, national unity, and the continuity of essential services.

The administration’s approach extended beyond political statements, with officials stressing the need to maintain economic activity, public services and infrastructure while the Armed Forces were engaged in military operations.
​
Pezeshkian has repeatedly described support for the Armed Forces as a responsibility of his administration. “Defending the country’s Armed Forces is my duty,” he said after the 12-day war.
​
The president has also emphasized national unity, saying that Iran’s resistance during the war brought together the people, Armed Forces, and government. He said the country’s enemies failed to achieve their objectives despite targeting military commanders, nuclear scientists, and infrastructure.
​
Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref likewise highlighted the role of the Defense Ministry and the country’s defense sector during the 12-day war, saying they had played “a special role” and that Iran possessed significant defense capabilities.
​
Aref also called for shortcomings in the country’s air-defense capabilities, particularly cybersecurity, to be addressed, indicating that the administration’s support for the Armed Forces was intended to include strengthening defense capabilities and addressing weaknesses.
​
The administration also sought to keep the country’s economic and administrative machinery operating during both wars. Officials stressed the importance of maintaining supplies, transportation, energy, healthcare, communications, and other essential services to prevent military pressure from developing into a wider domestic crisis.
​
In a September 2025 meeting with Pezeshkian and members of his cabinet, the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, praised administration officials and employees who had served during the 12-day war. He specifically commended government bodies that had “truly sacrificed” during the war and praised Pezeshkian’s motivation, morale, and hard work.
​
The late Leader also stressed the need to strengthen the components of national power and dignity and praised cooperation among the heads of the three branches of government.
​
The experience of the two wars demonstrated that national defense extends beyond the battlefield. While the Armed Forces carried out military defense, the administration sought to ensure that the country’s economic, administrative, and public-service systems remained operational, turning political support for the Armed Forces into a broader responsibility of governance.

🎙 Over 1,900 agriculture projects to be inaugurated across Iran: Minister

📌 Bandar Abbas, IRNA – Iran’s Agriculture Minister Gholamreza Nouri Ghezeljeh says 1,925 agricultural projects will be inaugurated across the country during this year’s Government Week that starts on August 24, with Hormozgan Province accounting for the largest share with 32 projects.

Speaking at a meeting of Hormozgan’s Planning Council on Thursday, Nouri Ghezeljeh said the projects include infrastructure and production schemes aimed at strengthening the agricultural sector and promoting a marine-based economy.
​
He said the administration has prioritized the development of coastal areas and the islands, with comprehensive plans being drawn up to make greater use of the country’s maritime capacities.
​
The minister also stressed the need to strengthen rural markets, support agricultural exports and reduce the role of unnecessary intermediaries in the supply chain. He said measures including agricultural insurance, price reforms and a rapid response to market problems are among the ministry’s priorities.
​
Nouri Ghezeljeh further highlighted the role of farmers, fishermen and other producers in maintaining Iran’s food security despite economic pressures, energy and water imbalances, drought and restrictions on maritime trade.
